method: built-in image_gen; one edit call per asset, no creative retries
paths: public/assets/ paths are relative to the repository root, where those files live today; ~ is the home directory of the machine that ran the edits, and the Codex sheets under it were never committed

entries.name: operation-tango
entries.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: a production 12-frame cartoon animation sprite sheet for a personal co-op games webpage.
Input image roles: Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the existing 4-column by 3-row animation sprite sheet. Image 2 is the EXISTING LOVERS STILL, the authoritative identity, facial design, body proportions and drawing-style reference for the boy. Image 3 is the EXISTING HEAVENLY STILL, a supporting reference for the girl's joyful facial expression.
Primary request: Redraw the characters across all twelve target frames consistently. The boy must look like exactly the boy from Image 2: same narrow friendly face, smooth straight brown side-swept undercut, distinctive glasses with black upper browline and slim silver lower rim, slim longer torso and limbs, and the same appealing simplified playful cartoon design. Adapt only his clothes to the target scene. Do not use the larger, spikier-haired boy design in the original Tango scene. These are young adults stylized in a playful rounded cartoon, not photoreal people. Keep the boy's recognizable face and slim body from the Lovers reference without exaggerating the head or cheeks.
The girl must be consistent across every scene, blending the compact athletic proportions and black ponytail of Image 2 with the expressive joyful face of Image 3. She is a shorter athletic Asian young adult with warm skin, a black ponytail, expressive dark eyes and a lively smile. Preserve recognizability and avoid an infant/toddler face. Use the same contour weight, soft painted shading and playful illustration style as the Lovers reference.
Technical composition: output ONE image, exactly 2048 pixels wide by 1536 pixels tall, arranged as EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS AND THREE ROWS of equal 512-by-512 SQUARE FRAMES. No margins, no gutters, no panel borders, no captions, no labels, no text, no watermarks. All 12 tiles must have identical camera size and complete uncropped scenes. Each tile fills its entire square. Chronological order is LEFT TO RIGHT, THEN TOP TO BOTTOM, frames 1 through 12. Preserve each original target frame's pose order, locations and main story actions. Keep background landmarks, lighting, scale and camera framing stable from frame to frame. Use small coherent animation movements and keep first and final frame very close for a smooth loop. Do not collapse the sheet into one picture or make rectangular frames. Render all twelve frames carefully.
Target scene: Operation Tango. Keep the full-frame split hacker/agent composition: boy on LEFT at dark laptop in coral-red hoodie over dark shirt, headset and glasses, girl on RIGHT in teal jacket and charcoal cargo pants with headset beside the glowing triangle door control. A bright vertical cyan divider separates warm hacker room and cool blue corridor. Keep their relative positions and the electronic door/laptop/triangle motifs.
Actions, preserve target chronology: Frame 1 both eager at their stations, frame 2 boy types and girl prepares, frames 3-4 girl presses the glowing triangle panel, frame 5 small success celebration, frame 6 they fist-bump across the divider, frames 7-8 both cheer with raised fists, frame 9 shared laugh, frame 10 return to stations, frames 11-12 return to the beginning pose. Keep playful co-op teamwork and the recognisable hacker/agent story. Apply the Lovers boy identity and the blended girl design consistently in EVERY frame.
